title: Carrie — Season 1
hook: The real horror begins with the people who make someone feel powerless.
review: Carrie remains a frightening story because its cruelty is recognisable long before anything supernatural happens.
The most disturbing people in the story are not necessarily those with unusual powers. They are ordinary people who find pleasure in humiliating somebody vulnerable.
The longer series format creates opportunities to examine that cruelty in greater detail.
Isolation, parental control and public embarrassment can slowly reshape how a person sees the world.
The modern setting also creates an interesting question about humiliation in the age of social media.
An embarrassing moment no longer needs to remain inside a school building. It can follow someone everywhere.
The danger of expanding a familiar horror story is explaining too much.
Fear sometimes becomes stronger when the audience does not fully understand what is coming.
The emotional foundation remains the most important element. Spectacle means little unless we understand the suffering behind it.
Hmm... a disturbing story about cruelty, power and the consequences of treating another person as entertainment.

Mike Flanagan's adaptation expands Stephen King's familiar tragedy into an eight-episode story. Summer H. Howell plays Carrie White, while Samantha Sloyan takes on Margaret, the mother whose controlling religious worldview shapes much of Carrie's suffering.

The modern setting changes the nature of humiliation. Cruelty can now travel through phones, photographs and social media, following a teenager beyond the school corridor. That gives the old story a frightening contemporary dimension.
Flanagan's strength is empathy. He wants viewers to understand why people behave as they do, including characters who might otherwise remain straightforward villains.

But empathy creates a difficult trade-off. If every terrible decision receives an explanation, the story risks losing some of its moral uncertainty. Understanding cruelty is not the same as excusing it.

The expanded story also introduces additional supernatural material, including Emaline. These choices create fresh dramatic possibilities but move the adaptation further from the simplicity of the original tragedy.

The prom sequence remains a major production undertaking, with elaborate practical effects and a large ensemble. Yet the most important part of Carrie is still the emotional journey leading to that catastrophe, not the scale of the destruction.
works: Psychological horror, themes of isolation, bullying, parental control and social cruelty.
misses: Potential overextension and reduced ambiguity compared with a more compact telling.
note: Original Movie....hmm editorial assessment based on available story information and critical discussion; not a firsthand screening.
editorialHeadline: THE REAL MONSTERS DON'T NEED SUPERNATURAL POWERS.
